#     _deck.scss   layout + slide types from the toolkit (generated)
#     _brand.scss  colours + fonts from brand.yml        (generated)
#     custom.scss  tweaks for THIS deck only             (yours — wins over the rest)
# (Quarto reads the *variables* of later files first, which is why the brand
#  tokens sit after the layout that uses them.)

title: "REPORT TITLE HERE"

    margin: 0
    menu: false
    progress: false
    auto-stretch: false
    fig-align: center

jupyter: python3

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from er_toolkit import brand
from er_toolkit.viz.mpl import chart_title, graded, bar_labels, add_baseline

b = brand.use(context="slide")     # reads ER_BRAND from _environment
# Colour a chart with the brand, never a hex:
#   b.primary.base / b.secondary.base     the brand colours
#   b.primary[300]                        any shade 50–900
#   graded(values)                        bars shaded light→dark by value
#   b.palette("categorical", n=4)         multi-series colours

# ── DEMO DATA — delete and load your own ──
seg  = ["Segment A", "Segment B", "Segment C", "Segment D", "Segment E"]
val  = [12.4, 9.1, 7.8, 6.2, 4.5]
val2 = [3.0, 4.2, 6.1, 5.0, 7.3]
BASE = 8.1
```

to a card to colour its number with the brand's risk colours.

## Part 2 — the drivers {.section-break data-kick="Part 2"}

A full-bleed divider. Use one per major section of a longer deck.

## Single chart {data-kick="Example · one chart"}

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.2))
bars = ax.bar(seg, val, color=graded(val), edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
bar_labels(ax, bars)
add_baseline(ax, BASE, label="Base {:.1f}")
chart_title(ax, "One chart, centred on a card", "Bars graded light → dark by value")
ax.set_ylabel("Demo metric"); ax.margins(y=0.16)
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — `graded()`, `bar_labels()`, `add_baseline()` and `chart_title()` all read the active brand.
:::

## Two figures side by side {data-kick="Example · two-up"}

```{python}
#| layout-ncol: 2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 4.4))
bars = ax.bar(seg, val, color=graded(val), edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
bar_labels(ax, bars, fontsize=9)
chart_title(ax, "A bar chart")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.margins(y=0.18); plt.show()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 4.4))
ax.plot(seg, val2, marker="o", color=b.secondary.base, linewidth=2.5)
chart_title(ax, "A trend line")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — `#| layout-ncol: 2` puts two independent figures on their own cards.
:::

## A text slide {data-kick="Example · text"}

Text-only slides centre themselves — no layout work needed.

- **Retained** — the drivers you're keeping
- **Parked** — what you set aside, and why
- **Next** — the one action you're asking for

::: {.caveat}
EXAMPLE — `.caveat` (secondary colour) for a watch-out; `.takeaway` (primary) for the key point.
:::

<script>
// Cover kicker + stat chips (edit or delete).
window.addEventListener('load', () => {
  const t = document.getElementById('title-slide');
  if (t && !t.querySelector('.cover-meta')) {
    const head = document.createElement('div');
    head.className = 'cover-head';
    head.innerHTML = '<div class="cover-kick">01 &nbsp;·&nbsp; Report Series</div><div class="cover-rule"></div>';
    t.insertBefore(head, t.firstChild);
    const d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className = 'cover-meta';
    d.innerHTML = `
      <div class="cm"><span class="cm-n">0000</span><span class="cm-l">Metric one</span></div>
      <div class="cm"><span class="cm-n">0.00</span><span class="cm-l">Metric two</span></div>
      <div class="cm"><span class="cm-n">0.0%</span><span class="cm-l">Metric three</span></div>`;
    t.appendChild(d);
  }
});
</script>
